extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimental scientists, and readers of the Philosophical Transactions / Royal Society members
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative guidance for reading, judging, and reporting on natural-philosophy / experimental papers and books (17th-century context): assessing novelty, experimental rigor, clarity of demonstration, and alignment with observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worthiness of extraction / relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: There is nothing in this paper that is worthy of being extracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A paper should contain material of sufficient interest or novelty to merit extraction or summary in the Transactions; if it lacks extractable content, it may be judged as not worth reporting. (Used here as a short negative judgment to indicate lack of substantive contribution.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and instructiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Of a piece with the other chemical papers of this author, prolix in the extreme, and wholly uninstructive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excessive prolixity; contributions should be concise and carry instructive content. Long-winded exposition that fails to instruct is an anti-pattern and grounds for negative evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental controls and exclusion of confounders
rubrics_metrics.description: He having taken extraordinary care and pains to observe, that always on the flesh before it did verminate, there sat flies of the self-same kind with those that were afterwards produced thence; and again, that no worms would ever come from any flesh in vessels well covered, and defended from the access of flies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments to exclude alternative sources/agents (e.g., prevent access of flies), use covered controls, and observe whether the putative causal agent is present; explicit controls that rule out confounders are required to support causal claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of inventive control variants to test alternative explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Lest it should be objected that the reason why, in vessels exactly closed, no insect breeds, is the want of air necessary to all generation, he has carefully covered several vessels with very fine Naples veil, for the air to enter though flies could not; but that no worms at all were bred there, notwithstanding that many flies swarmed about them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate objections and implement variant controls (e.g., allow air but prevent vector access) to distinguish between competing explanations (air availability vs vector deposition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication, seasonality, and contextual conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is no wonder that Dr. Tonge's experiments, concerning the bleeding of the sycamore, do not agree with ours, they being made in a different season; his in February, and ours towards the end of March.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report timing, seasonal and environmental conditions; discrepancies between experiments may be explained by differences in season or context. Replicate experiments across relevant conditions and record those conditions explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative experiments under matched conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The experiments concerning the northern and southern sides of sycamores were made at the same time; and are well solved by the same hypothesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing treatments or sides, perform observations simultaneously or under matched conditions so that comparisons are meaningful and hypotheses can be properly tested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative measurement and descriptive detail
rubrics_metrics.description: From a wine quart of the salt spring at East Chenock ... he obtained by evaporation near 80 grains of salt ... by dissolving two grains of the salt of iron in four ounces of common water, and adding a given proportion of gall, it appeared of the same colour, yielded the same precipitate, and had the same taste as the Farrington waters when so treated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative measures (weights, volumes, proportions) and descriptive observations (colour, precipitate, taste) so that experiments can be compared, reproduced, and evaluated; give enough detail of procedures and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of construction, demonstration, and exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction. (Fig. 2, PI. xi.) ... Demonstration. — Bishop Ward ... gives a method ... In the triangle SFT, are given, SF the distance of the foci; FT = FE + ES = AP; and AFT, the external angle or mean anomaly, equal to the sum of the angles FST and T: Therefore the angle FSE, or the true anomaly, = the difference of the angles FST and T, may be found thus: ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear step-by-step constructions and demonstrations (with figures where appropriate), state givens explicitly, and derive results logically so readers can follow and verify the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical rigor vs geometric/diagrammatic methods — trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: To grant what is true, viz. that the geometrical delineation of M. Cassini is somewhat more expeditious; yet, should we aim at that accuracy which astronomers desire, it might be feared it would require very large diagrams, and become more operose than the calculus itself. But if we make use of this, we shall find both methods to be equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess methods for accuracy, labor, and practicality: diagrammatic approaches may be faster but can become unwieldy for high precision; analytic/calculus methods may be more compact or accurate. Evaluate and justify method choice based on desired accuracy and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of hypothesis with observations; willingness to revise
rubrics_metrics.description: Kepler himself was of this opinion ... But, when he found that this did not agree with his observations, he changed his mind, and maintained that the line of the true motion of a planet described equal elliptical areas in equal times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theories must be tested against observations and revised when they fail to match empirical data. Intellectual flexibility and readiness to amend hypotheses in light of evidence is a positive evaluative criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generality and constancy of empirical patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: He positively affirms, that he could never find, by all the experiments and observations he ever made ... that any insects were ever bred from flesh ... he observes, that both the generation of worms in vegetables is always and constantly the same (not at all casual), and that all galls grow constantly in one determinate part of the branches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer results that demonstrate consistent, repeatable patterns across many instances; document regularities (species-specific associations, recurring locations) rather than isolated or casual occurrences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple observations / many experiments to support a conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: He relates a great number of [experiments] made by himself upon all sorts of animals ... and that no worms would ever come from any flesh in vessels well covered ... having taken extraordinary care and pains to observe ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support claims with numerous independent observations or experiments; single observations are weaker evidence. Thorough empirical support increases confidence in conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation of alternative causal mechanisms (physical vs geometric causes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some have blamed Kepler as giving way too much to physical causes, and swerving from geometry: as if physical causes were inconsistent with it; or, as if the problem were too ungeometrical, which, without mentioning physical causes, is thus proposed: The area of the trilinear figure intercepted between the line of the apses and that of the true motion, and the elliptical periphery, being given; to find the angle at the sun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and discuss the roles of physical interpretation versus mathematical formulation; explicitly state which causal or mathematical perspective is being used and defend its appropriateness for the problem.
